messages.content: 如果我從紐約出發，前往洛杉磯，然後從洛杉磯前往邁阿密，最後從邁阿密返回紐約，總共的距離是多少公里？

function.name: geo_distance_calculate
function.description: Calculate the geographic distance between two given locations. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_location.description: The starting location for the distance calculation.

end_location.description: The destination location for the distance calculation.

units.description: Optional. The desired units for the resulting distance ('miles' or 'kilometers'). Defaults to 'miles'.

The user asks: "If I start from New York, go to Los Angeles, then from LA to Miami, and finally from Miami back to New York, what is the total distance in kilometers?" We need to calculate distances between NYC to LA, LA to Miami, Miami to NYC. Use the geo_distance_calculate function. Provide arguments: start_location, end_location, units='kilometers'.

We need to call the function three times? Or we can combine into one? The function calculates distance between two points; we need to compute each leg separately.

So first leg: start_location="New York", end_location="Los Angeles". Then second leg: start_location="Los Angeles", end_location="Miami". Third leg: start_location="Miami", end_location="New York".

We should call the function thrice. But maybe we can pass multiple calls? The function signature expects a single pair. So we need to call it three times. We'll do separate calls.

We'll produce JSON with function calls. According to guidelines, we should output a single JSON object with name and arguments. But we have multiple calls. The guidelines say: "When calling a function, you must provide a JSON object with the following format: {name: ..., arguments: ...}". It doesn't specify how to handle multiple calls. Usually we can chain them sequentially. But we might need to call them one after another. In this environment, we can make multiple calls. Let's just call the function once per leg. We'll produce three calls. But the system may only accept one function call at a time. However, we can produce a single function call that includes all legs? No, the function only accepts start_location and end_location. So we need to call it three times. We can do so by making three separate calls. We'll produce them sequentially.

Thus:

First call: name=geo_distance_calculate, arguments={start_location:"New York", end_location:"Los Angeles", units:"kilometers"}.

Second call: name=geo_distance_calculate, arguments={start_location:"Los Angeles", end_location:"Miami", units:"kilometers"}.

Third call: name=geo_distance_calculate, arguments={start_location:"Miami", end_location:"New York", units:"kilometers"}.

But we need to output them as separate messages? The guidelines: "When calling a function, you must provide a JSON object with the following format: {name: ..., arguments: ...}. Do not add any additional text." So we can't include explanatory text. So we need to output exactly the JSON. For multiple calls, we might need to output them one after another. But the system might interpret only the last call. It's ambiguous. Perhaps we can combine them into a single function call that returns an array of distances? But the function signature doesn't support that. So we need to call thrice. We'll produce three separate function calls. The system will process them sequentially.

Thus we output:

{
"name":"geo_distance_calculate",
"arguments":{
"start_location":"New York",
"end_location":"Los Angeles",
"units":"kilometers"
}
}

Then next call etc. But we cannot put multiple JSON objects in one message. So we need to send them one by one. We'll do that.
